notes: Each configuration ran once per eval (the '3 runs each' label is the script's default text; n=1).

Evals 3 (supersede) and 4 (.adr-dir detection) passed 6/6 in BOTH configs — with a strong baseline model and existing ADRs in the repo to imitate, these scenarios do not discriminate. They still guard against regressions.

The skill's value concentrates where there is no example to imitate: eval 1 fresh repo (7/7 vs 3/7 — baseline skipped the adr init seed, used docs/adr instead of doc/adr, added non-canonical ### subsections, and invented two claims about MongoDB/team experience) and eval 2 vague request (4/4 vs 3/4 — baseline wrote a numbered skeleton ADR into the log instead of asking first; it did ask good questions and marked TODOs).

Baseline's eval-1 fabrications ('team has less operational experience with MongoDB transactions', 'not its primary design center') are exactly the failure mode the skill's record-don't-invent contract targets.
Cost of the skill: +6.9k tokens (~+59%) and +11.4s per invocation, from reading SKILL.md + references/examples.md.
All four with-skill runs produced byte-clean adr-tools format (single-blank-line discipline, exact supersede link scheme with modern 'Superseded' spelling, minimal one-line diff to the old ADR).
